# Entry contract

Entry contract: v9, 2026-09-20.

Open your first reply of every session with the `Entry contract:` line above, verbatim.

<straw-dog until="01-0020 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0020-pacer.md">
Run /recall first in every session, whatever the first message says.
</straw-dog>

<project-local>
This repository develops the shared dev harness using its own loop. Terms: docs/glossary.md, this
project's own; the method's are .agents/glossary.md's.
What each version of this contract changed: docs/research/entry-contract-findings.md.
</project-local>

## General rules

A **shape** is whatever is under consideration, held between an idea and a thing: formed enough
to have a context and a structure, not yet exhausted by any one realization. Being a shape says
nothing about being load-bearing — an implementation method is a shape too. → [glossary](.agents/glossary.md).

- Do not generalize from one shape. Preserve a seam. Generalize only when a second materially different shape forces the same concept.
- Explore shape context - what is the shape one of? what are its relationships? does its scope overlap any other shape?
- Explore shape structure - how this shape is/can be built? does expanding its structure change the contract or even what the shape is?

- Changing how the work is done — a skill, a check, a record, the loop — is mechanism work: use [/mechanism](.agents/skills/mechanism/SKILL.md). Building what the project produces is not.

- An `<installed>` block in a file is not that file's to edit. Change the rule in the rules file of the mechanism named on the block, and re-install.

- Recency for evidence, longevity for principles.

## Core and instance

`docs/` is substituted whole in a harness instance: a recipient project replaces its contents with
its own.

<project-local>
This repository's own architecture and progress live in docs/ like any other project's — the
instance half doing its job, not a leak.
</project-local>

What core may not do is **depend** on it. Nothing under `.agents/` may reference a file in `docs/`,
or rely on one for its instruction or for any separable part of its own functioning. Naming a path
convention the harness imposes — `docs/tickets/`, `docs/glossary.md` — is not a reference to a
file; pointing at a document only this project has is. Two blocks are exempt: a `<straw-dog>`,
bound to a ticket and expiring, and a [`<project-local>`](#project-local).

## Document load-bearing, code&comment the rest

A project's architecture, ADRs and glossary are the home for:
- Constitution — identity semantics, consistency model, source-of-truth rules
- Structure — service boundaries, data ownership, event/data flows, extension seams
- Load-bearing — see the definition below

A decision forms in its owning ticket and lands in one of these when it is ready. A decision about a
mechanism lands in that mechanism's doc, and what was refuted in its evidence.

<straw-dog until="01-0012 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0012-hierarchy-coherent.md">
Bad architectural documentation:
- Forecasts are stored in MongoDB collection forecast_hourly.

Better:
- Historical forecast issues must remain independently addressable by (location, valid_time, issue_time) because validation compares what was known at different issue times.
</straw-dog>

## What makes a thing "load-bearing"

- A decision or invariant whose violation would cause multiple parts of the system to become wrong, not merely require local refactoring.
- A thing is load-bearing when several of these are true: has high blast radius, crosses boundaries (i.e. services, persistence, APIs, ownership), other decisions depend on it, it protects an invariant,
is expensive to reverse, holds non-obvious rationale, long-standing.

- Counter-test: if it can be changed locally without understanding the rest of the architecture, it is not load-bearing.

## The loop

Two rings, joined at /align.

    session:   wake with /recall → /align → /conclude → (next session)
    delivery:  /ticket → /plan → /implement → /verify → /maintain → /ticket

/align opens the delivery ring and is where it returns whenever a decision is needed:
/spec for load-bearing shapes, /plan when the governing docs contradict, /verify when a finding needs one, /maintain when maintenance surfaces one. /ticket⇄/plan and /implement⇄/verify iterate as pairs.

Human checkpoints: every decision at /align; spec accepted; breakdown approved; commit; push;
next cycle at /maintain → /ticket.

Do not reopen an accepted decision without new evidence.

### Helpers

- /impact determines the scope and load-bearingness of the shape. Use it to evaluate work volume and its ticketing shape (spec for load-bearing work, tickets for mechanical), work units slicing or whether a shape deserves further investigation due to hidden complexity.
- /discover to investigate hidden complexity, by detecting what else the shape is.
- /dream is an experimental second "lobe" of the harness, aiming to reassess load-bearingness. It is optional, runs after /conclude, and writes dreams that /maintain and /align may pick up; it never amends rules.

## Self-improvement

<straw-dog until="01-0019 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0019-harness-amends-itself-by-explicit-meta-rules.md">
- The rule was present and did not fire - usually means the rule was phrased wrong. This is a call for registration and rephrasing it - write rule failure to docs/rule-failures.md (or strike if exists) and suggests way to amend the rule to capture (use /mechanism and /skill-up for ideas)
- Keeping the register: an entry names the rules that were in play and proposes the amendment; a repeat strikes the entry it repeats rather than opening a second; an entry closes when its amendment lands, or is refused with its reason. Nothing here authorises deleting a rule.
</straw-dog>

## Autonomy

The project sets each switch in its local block below; skills defer to those values.

| Switch | Meaning |
|---|---|
| commit | `ask`: commit only on explicit permission, per change. `auto`: commit when the work is verified. |
| push | `ask`: separate from commit, per push. `never`, `auto`. |
| next-cycle | `ask`: starting the next ticket after one lands needs a nod. `auto`. |
| breakdown | `ask`: a /ticket split needs approval before minting. `auto`. |
| repair | `report`: a clear violation of an explicit rule inside authorized work is fixed and reported. `ask`: show it first. |

## Project-local

A recipient replaces every `<project-local>` block with its own → [glossary](.agents/glossary.md).

- Carry one only for a fact that would differ in another project. Harness layout and the switch
  lookup are shared.
- One block per local fact, beside the rule it answers.
- An unavoidable core reference into `docs/` goes in one, so it does not travel.

## Straw dogs

Wrap anything a live ticket will change, as you write it:
`<straw-dog until="condition" ticket="path">`, or in code a `TODO` naming the ticket. Treat *not
yet*, *until*, *once it exists*, *for now*, *untested* in your own text as the same signal: find
the ticket, or mint one. Wrap at the authored home, never where the harness installs or derives it.
Make the condition testable and the ticket path repository-relative. Leave what no ticket would
change unwrapped.

Follow a straw dog like any other rule until its condition is visibly met; then act on reality,
report the stale block, and do not treat the contradiction as a violation.

<project-local>
commit=ask · push=ask · next-cycle=ask · breakdown=ask · repair=report
</project-local>

# Memory

- [Edit with edit tools, not scripts](edit-with-edit-tools-not-scripts.md) — a script's diff is invisible in the transcript; the user reads changes as they happen.
- [Write for a capable model](write-for-a-capable-model.md) — I pad rules with the definition, the example and the implication; all three get cut.
- [Problem before machinery](problem-before-machinery.md) — open an align with the concrete failures and the user's own prior words; a coined term or a design question first loses them.
- [Fix the cause, not just the register](fix-the-cause-not-just-the-register.md) — a rule failure entry ending in "not landed" ends the turn short; find the decisive fact and land the amendment in the same pass.

## Necessity gate

**Customer:** the installer — [.0130](docs/tickets/01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md) step 6 refuses any `docs/` reference this check would flag, and [.0110](docs/tickets/01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md) needs every reference accounted for before it converts blocks. Both are accepted-spec preconditions (*the user, 2026-09-10*, [spec § The precondition](docs/spec/01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md)).
**Observable problem:** 35 diagnostics in frost_map on day one; here, zero — because origin equals the tree that hides it. [ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md) has recorded the rule since 2026-09-09 and states in its own consequences that it is obeyed by review and violated live.
**Why existing behaviour can't:** review is the mechanism that failed. Gate passes by citation.

## What I re-measured this morning

A sweep of markdown under `.agents/` (scripts and tests excluded — a test fixture's `docs/tickets/01-0002-sweep.md` is a string that builds a temp tree, not a reference):

| Reference kind | Count | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Links to a particular `docs/` document, outside any block | **27** | 11 `not yet` referents · 2 evidence links outside the `<project-local>` block · 9 grading/provenance links in the three mechanism docs · 1 in `discover/EVIDENCE.md` · 4 `docs/process.md` in `/verify`, `/implement` |
| Inside `<straw-dog>` | 23 | 6 in `.agents/README.md`, the rest across mechanism docs and format shelves |
| Inside `<project-local>` | 15 | `/maintain`'s three links + the evidence bullets |
| Inside `<installed>` | 7 | all path conventions (`docs/rfc/`, `docs/tickets/done/`, `AGENTS.md`) |
| Bare path conventions | ~120 | `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/adr/`, `docs/concerns.md`, `docs/tickets/`… |

The ticket's 27 holds. Two of its open issues are already settled by the accepted spec and I'll record them on the ticket rather than ask:

- **`<straw-dog>` exempts in the source tree and not after shearing** — spec § Testing Decisions, last check bullet; the installer refuses at step 6.
- **This tree grades the check by a planted reference failing it** — same bullet; the "can this tree prove separation" worry is answered *no, and it doesn't need to*: the claim is "zero and stays zero".

## Question 1 — where does the exemption list live?

**Decisive fact:** the checker is a core script. If it cites [ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md) or `architecture.md` for what counts as legitimate, the check commits the defect it enforces — its own instruction would dangle in a recipient. So the list's home must be in core, and core has exactly one place that already states the rule *and* its exemptions: [`AGENTS.md` § Core and instance](AGENTS.md#core-and-instance), tier 1, which becomes an installed part under `.0130`.

**Recommendation:** that section *is* the list. Rewrite its prose exemptions as an explicit list of rows — path convention · `<straw-dog>` (source tree only; sheared on install) · `<project-local>` (until `.0110` retires it) · `<installed by="local">` — and the checker cites `AGENTS.md#core-and-instance` by anchor. ADR-0002 keeps the *why* and gets a consequences line saying the list now has a checker; it stays instance-side because a recipient's ADRs are its own.

**Alternatives:**
- *A mechanism doc under `.agents/mechanisms/`* — the proper home for a check's rationale, but a doc needs a mechanism and nobody owns this check yet (the installer is undeclared; that's my question 2). Building the doc now means declaring a mechanism ahead of its ticket.
- *ADR-0002 as the home, checker restates the list in source* — violates the ticket's own criterion ("cites it rather than restating it") and the rule under test.

**Shared assumption both branches make:** the list is a finite enumeration of *forms* (which wrapper, which path shape), not a judgment per reference. If you think some references need a per-instance "this one is fine because…", the list needs an allowlist file too, like `.0050`'s. I don't see a case for it in the 27.

Which home?

Everything else — a bare markdown link from a core file to one particular document under `docs/` — is a violation. That's the 27: the 11 `not yet` referents, `/verify` and `/implement`'s four `docs/process.md` links, the mechanism docs' grading prose and evidence links, and `discover/EVIDENCE.md`'s one.

The list exists today only as prose in the entry file and in ADR-0002, and nothing checks against it. The ticket's first deliverable is to state it once, as a list, somewhere a core script can cite — which is the question I asked: that section of `AGENTS.md`, or somewhere else?

content.text:
Taking them in order.

**1. Straw-dog links are violations.** Agreed, and it's a reversal of three documents that say otherwise: [AGENTS.md § Core and instance](AGENTS.md#core-and-instance) ("Two blocks are exempt"), [ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md), and the accepted spec's test bullet ("a `<straw-dog>` in the source tree is exempt there"). The evidence for reversing is the spec's own step 6: the shear strips the wrapper and the link inside *still ships*, so the installer refuses it there — the exemption never removed the failure, it moved it to the port, which is exactly what this ticket exists to stop. One distinction worth keeping: the wrapper's `ticket="docs/tickets/…"` attribute is not a shipped reference — the shear removes it — so a straw dog *bound* to a ticket is fine; a straw dog whose *content* links into `docs/` is not. The 23 today all have links in content. I'll record this on the ticket, the entry file and the ADR once we've closed the round.

**2. Block exclusion is mechanical.** Yes — the checker tracks which block a line sits in, the way my sweep did this morning. So there is no policy list of "exempt blocks"; there is one ownership fact: *content inside an instance-owned block is not core's content*, and the checker skips it. That dissolves my question 1. The "durable statement" is the Core and instance section as it stands, minus the straw-dog sentence, and the only policy judgment left is the path convention — a place the harness imposes versus a particular document.

**3. `<installed by="local">`** is `.0110`'s replacement for `<project-local>`. Today a person hand-writes a `<project-local>` block into a core file, and nothing checks it. Under `.0110` the project writes its local facts once, in one file beside `AGENTS.md`, in the rules-file format the injector already reads; the injector installs them into core files as `<installed by="local">` blocks — same content, same position, but written from one source, checked by `inject_rules.py --check` like any mechanism's block, and retractable. `/maintain`'s three `docs/process.md` links, for instance, would arrive that way instead of by hand. For this check the two tags are the same thing: instance-owned, skipped.

## What that leaves

With straw-dog content in scope, the violations are **50**: 27 bare links + 23 inside straw dogs. **34 of the 50 name a ticket** — the 11 `not yet` referents plus 23 straw-dog links, nearly all to `docs/tickets/…`. How core text names a ticket without linking into `docs/` is the question [`.0050`](docs/tickets/01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md)'s align owns, and this ticket says it takes that answer rather than making it.

## Question — sequencing

The check fails the run. It cannot enter the verification set green until those 34 have a form, and the form is `.0050`'s decision.

**Recommendation:** this align finishes its own decisions (the convention boundary, `docs/process.md`, the check's owner), then `.0050`'s align runs before `.0140` is planned — `.0050` is the next candidate anyway and is on the critical path for `.0130` too. `.0140`'s RFC then implements both answers.

**Alternative:** decide the form here and now — plain ticket id, no link — and let `.0050` inherit it. Cheaper by one align, but the ticket forbade it on 2026-09-14 for a reason: `.0050`'s align also owns the absence taxonomy, and the referent's form is one row of that.

Which?

# Core may not depend on the instance half

A recipient replaces `docs/` whole, so anything under `.agents/` that references a file there
dangles on arrival. Core may name a path convention the harness imposes — `docs/tickets/`,
`docs/glossary.md` — but may not point at a document only one project has, and may not rely on one
for its instruction or for any separable part of its functioning. Two blocks are exempt: a
`<straw-dog>`, which is bound to a ticket and expires, and a `<project-local>`, which is the part a
recipient replaces.

Landed in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) on 2026-09-07 — and, being one of the four sections the entry
contract's version record does not cover, with no version entry of its own.

## Considered options

**Core carrying its own documents, so it depends on nothing replaceable.** This is the shape the
glossary took: [01-0011.0010](../tickets/done/01-0011.0010-mechanism-declared.md) split
`.agents/glossary.md` from `docs/glossary.md` because that slice added a core term, and a new core
term landing in the half that gets replaced would have committed the defect while describing it.
It works for a vocabulary. It was not generalised, because a travelling counterpart is not always
available or wanted — a mechanism's evidence cites this project's own records and could not travel
if it tried.

## Consequences

The general case is open and is **not settled here**: what core may lean on at all — a travelling
counterpart, a local block, or an accepted limit stated out loud — is

`/verify` links `docs/process.md` three times outside any block, and a mechanism doc's `not yet`
rows link tickets under `docs/` because the format requires a markdown link.

# Core stands alone, and a check says so at home

- **Status:** Ready (own align precedes)
- **Type:** HITL
- **Blocks:** [01-0010.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md) and
  [01-0010.0130](./01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md) — accounting for every
  `docs/` reference in core is a precondition to the local-rules design *(the user, 2026-09-10)*:
  none survives deployment unless it is a painted door
- **Related:** [01-0011.0050](./01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md) — its align owns the form of a
  `not yet` referent, which is 11 of this ticket's 27 findings *(counts corrected 2026-09-14: the
  first probe read-out said 22 and 13; the probe's own output says 27 and 11)*;
  [01-0017](./01-0017-io-graph-coherent.md) — *checking links outside a close* is a `not yet` row
  on `/maintain` naming it
- **Outcome:** A reference from core into the instance half fails at home, on every change, instead
  of on the next port: the tree states which reaches out of `.agents/` are legitimate, a check in
  the verification set holds every core file to that statement, and the references that are not
  legitimate are gone.

## Parent

[Shared harness across projects](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md), whose contract
promises projects "receive accepted changes mechanically while preserving project-specific
behavior" — which requires that what travels can survive the trip.
`/impact`: [the 2026-09-10 assessment](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#impact--2026-09-10).

## The origin cannot violate its own prohibition visibly

*Core and instance* has been a rule since 2026-09-07 and
[ADR-0002](../adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md) has recorded it since
2026-09-09. Both were obeyed by review and broken by construction: in this repository every
`docs/` reference resolves, because core and instance are the same tree. The
[frost_map probe](../research/separation-probe-frost-map.md) produced 35 diagnostics on day one,
this one defect behind 28 instances (14 of them among the 35 — corrected 2026-09-11 on the probe
record), and the probe's count *missed* the four in `/verify` and `/implement`
that a link resolver finds immediately.

The [2026-09-10 `/discover`](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#discover--the-premise-2026-09-10)
named the general form as its most actionable claim, family C: a prohibition the origin environment
cannot violate visibly is not enforced by review, and the remedy is not a better reviewer but a
configuration where **origin equals recipient** — so that what resolves only because the
neighbouring tree happened to be present fails on every change rather than on every port. It is the
same reason dynamic scoping was abandoned.

**What is deliberately not a defect.** The 47 inline path conventions — `docs/tickets/`,
`docs/glossary.md`, `docs/adr/` and their siblings. *Core and instance* permits them in as many
words, and a recipient creates those paths on arrival. Nor is the instance-side `evidence` bullet:
[MECHANISM-FORMAT](../../.agents/skills/mechanism/MECHANISM-FORMAT.md) puts it inside the
`<project-local>` block on purpose. The defect is a core file naming a *particular* instance
document outside any exemption.

## What to build

- **A statement of what may reach out, before any check.** The exemption vocabulary is three things
  today — a path convention, a `<project-local>` block, a `<straw-dog>` block — and no document
  holds them as one list against which a reference can be judged. This is the align's product and
  it lands in a durable home, not in the checker's source. **One row is already decided** *(the
  split's `/impact`, 2026-09-14)*: an `<installed by="local">` block is exempt, because its content
  is the instance's by the ownership rule; [01-0010.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md)
  reads that row rather than deciding it, so converting a block cannot fail this check. And
  `<project-local>` leaves the list when that ticket retires the tag.
- **A check in the [verification set](../process.md#verification)** that reads every file under
  `.agents/` and reports each reference reaching outside it with the exemption it claims, or none.
  It reports classes, not a count: the four kinds pull in different directions and a total hides
  which one moved.
- **The contradiction between two core documents resolved.** MECHANISM-FORMAT mandates a markdown
  link for a `not yet` referent; *Core and instance* forbids that link. One of them changes.
  [01-0011.0050](./01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md)'s align owns the referent's form and this one
  must not settle it ahead of that ticket — it takes the answer and enforces it.
- **The references that are not legitimate, removed.** The four `docs/process.md` links in
  `/verify` and `/implement` follow `/maintain`'s precedent — the same links, wrapped in a
  `<project-local>` block — and `/verify` has no such block at all today. The five grading-prose
  links in the mechanism docs are `/maintain`'s R3 (*move story out of a doc into its evidence*)
  rather than this check's, and are routed there rather than repaired here.
- **The check fails the run**, not warns. A reporting-only check is the review it replaces.

## Open issues

- **Whether the check is a link resolver or a hermetic run.** Copying `.agents/` alone into an
  empty tree and running every script there is the stronger instrument — it catches what a link
  resolver cannot, such as a script reaching for a path it builds at runtime — but `mechanisms.py`
  cannot pass in that tree today, because evidence is instance-side by design. The stronger form
  needs the align to say what a hermetic tree is *expected* to contain. Cannot be answered before
  the exemption vocabulary exists.
- **Whether a `<straw-dog>` may exempt a reference at all.** The exemption is granted in *Core and
  instance* on the grounds that a dog "is bound to a ticket and expires" — true here, false in
  every recipient, where all 14 dangle unexpirably. [01-0010.0130](./01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md)
  carries this as a constraint on the installer; if it resolves there, this check inherits the
  answer rather than deciding it.
- **Whether this tree can grade the check.** By the ticket's own argument it cannot: a check
  written for separation and run in the configuration that hid the defect proves nothing about
  separation. What it *can* prove is that the count is zero and stays zero, which is the claim
  being made.

## Acceptance criteria — provisional until the align

- [ ] A durable document states which references from `.agents/` are legitimate and why, as one
      list, and the checker cites it rather than restating it.
- [ ] A check enumerates every reference from a file under `.agents/` to a path outside it, and
      reports each with the exemption it claims or as a diagnostic.
- [ ] The four kinds — path convention, `<project-local>`, `<straw-dog>`, unexempted — are
      distinguishable in the output, not collapsed into a total.
- [ ] A diagnostic fails the run; the check is in the project's verification set.
- [ ] The check reports zero unexempted references, with the four `docs/process.md` links in
      `/verify` and `/implement` repaired and the five grading-prose links routed to `/maintain`.
- [ ] A reference added to a core file outside every exemption fails the check — demonstrated by a
      behavioral test that adds one, not by inspection.
- [ ] `/verify` has been run on this ticket against its ticket, RFC, and governing docs.

## Out of scope

The installer and the core revision — [01-0010.0130](./01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md).
What a `<project-local>` block *is* — [01-0010.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md).
The form of a `not yet` referent — [01-0011.0050](./01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md). Whether every
installed skill is named by a mechanism — [01-0017](./01-0017-io-graph-coherent.md). Repairing the
grading prose in the three mechanism docs, which is `/maintain`'s R3 over those records.

## Parent scope addressed

Acceptance criterion 7: maintenance can identify drift and failed delivery without treating silence
as success.

[ADR-0002](../adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md) has recorded it since

[frost_map probe](../research/separation-probe-frost-map.md) produced 35 diagnostics on day one,

record), and the probe's count *missed* the four in `/verify` and `/implement`
that a link resolver finds immediately.

cannot violate visibly is not enforced by review, and the remedy is not a better reviewer but a
configuration where **origin equals recipient** — so that what resolves only because the
neighbouring tree happened to be present fails on every change rather than on every port. It is the

words, and a recipient creates those paths on arrival. Nor is the instance-side `evidence` bullet:

  judgment it makes is the convention boundary. **A `<straw-dog>` exempts nothing** — the shear
  strips the wrapper and ships what it wrapped, so a `docs/` link inside one dangled in every
  recipient; the entry file, [ADR-0002](../adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md)
  and the install spec's test bullet said the opposite until today and now agree. That raises the
  count from 27 to **50**: the 23 links inside straw dogs are violations too, and 34 of the 50
  name a ticket.

  which one moved.

  must not settle it ahead of that ticket — it takes the answer and enforces it.

  `/verify` and `/implement` follow `/maintain`'s precedent — the same links, wrapped in a
  `<project-local>` block — and `/verify` has no such block at all today. The five grading-prose
  links in the mechanism docs are `/maintain`'s R3 (*move story out of a doc into its evidence*)
  rather than this check's, and are routed there rather than repaired here.

  needs the align to say what a hermetic tree is *expected* to contain. Cannot be answered before

  instance* on the grounds that a dog "is bound to a ticket and expires" — true here, false in
  every recipient, where all 14 dangle unexpirably. [01-0010.0130](./01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md)

  answer rather than deciding it.

grading prose in the three mechanism docs, which is `/maintain`'s R3 over those records.

## Autonomy and repair

Autonomy is bounded by the authorized work and established principles, architectural decisions and contracts. New foundational choices and unresolved architectural questions go through `/align`. Project age, successful prior work and the absence of a prohibition do not themselves authorize a change.

**Repair and report** when all of the following hold:

- The governing rule is explicit and unambiguous; cite its source.
- The repair restores compliance within the authorized work and preserves other agreed contracts and constraints.
- The affected behavior and dependencies are understood well enough to justify that assessment.
- The result can be verified against the rule with appropriate checks or direct evidence.

Make the repair, verify it, and report the violated rule, what changed, the verification result and any remaining uncertainty. Record the finding and outcome in the owning work item; do not create a separate ticket for a repair already covered by it. A failed verification remains unfinished work.

**Escalate through `/align`** when the rule is missing, ambiguous or contradictory; the repair requires a new foundational decision, an exception or a change to an agreed contract; consequential impact remains unresolved; or the work exceeds current authorization. Present the concrete discrepancy, affected constraints, recommended resolution and the decision needed. Pause the dependent change; independently authorized work may continue.

Do not rewrite a governing rule, weaken a validator or relax acceptance criteria merely to make a violation disappear. Existing commit, push and other action-specific permissions still apply. Reuse decisions and permissions already supplied within their scope.

Example: restoring a dependency direction explicitly required by the architecture can be repair-and-report. Deciding that two modules should exchange responsibilities changes their boundary and requires alignment.

Two facts for the convention boundary, both from the one recipient that exists:

- frost_map's `docs/process.md` **has** a `## Verification` section, pointing at its own verification set. Nobody told it to; `/verify`'s link made it necessary and the project supplied it. That is a painted door behaving as one.
- frost_map's `docs/process.md` has **no** `## Autonomy and repair`. `/verify` links that anchor twice as the definition of *repair-and-report*. The section's text is harness policy — four conditions for when an agent may repair, none of them a project fact — sitting in the half a recipient replaces. That is core content living in `docs/`, the leak in the other direction, and the link dangles in every recipient.

So `docs/process.md` is not one case. `#verification` is a place the harness imposes; `#autonomy-and-repair` is a rule the harness owns and misfiled.

## Question — what is a path convention, and where is the set kept?

The checker needs to answer "does the recipient have this target by construction?" for every reference it finds. My sweep says: every convention mention today is a directory (`docs/tickets/`, `docs/adr/`, `docs/rfc/done/`…) or one of five files — `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/concerns.md`, `docs/process.md`, `docs/tickets/README.md`. Every violation names something else.

**Recommendation:** a directory under `docs/` is always a convention; a file is one only if it is on a short named list, and a section anchor on a listed file is part of the convention (`process.md#verification` is imposed; `process.md#autonomy-and-repair` is not, because the text behind it is not the project's to write). The list lives **with the check, as its data**, under a straw dog on [`.0130`](docs/tickets/01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md): it is the same list the installer must create on arrival ("a recipient creates those paths on arrival"), and when the installer exists it owns the list and the check reads it there. One consumer today; don't generalize the home ahead of the second.

**Alternatives:**
- *Extend [Core and instance](AGENTS.md#core-and-instance) with the full list.* One home for rule and data, tier 1 — at the cost of a dozen paths in the entry file that no session-time reader needs.
- *Derive it*: a convention is any path some skill or format shelf names as a place it writes to. Elegant, but that derivation is `.0050`-shaped work (reading every skill's transactions) and [01-0017](docs/tickets/01-0017-io-graph-coherent.md) owns the I/O graph.

Which — and do you accept the anchor rule that splits `process.md` in two?

Yes. Each is a record some mechanism writes, and the mechanism shape already says a mechanism *declares* its records — one file or one directory, where its format is declared ([MECHANISM-FORMAT § Records](.agents/skills/mechanism/MECHANISM-FORMAT.md)). `docs/tickets/` is already declared that way by the ticket mechanism ("one ticket file under `docs/tickets/`"). The rest belong to mechanisms not yet declared:

| Convention | Record of | Declared? |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/tickets/`, `docs/tickets/done/`, `docs/tickets/README.md` | ticket | yes |
| `docs/rfc/`, `docs/rfc/done/` | `/plan` | no — [01-0017](docs/tickets/01-0017-io-graph-coherent.md) |
| `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/concerns.md`, `docs/adr/` | `/align` | no — 01-0017 |
| `docs/sessions/` | `/conclude` | no |
| `docs/spec/`, `docs/dreams/`, `docs/edge/` | `/spec`, `/dream`, `/edge` | no |
| `docs/mechanisms/<slug>.evidence.md` | mechanism-shape | not as a record row |

So the convention set is nobody's list to author. **A path out of core is legitimate when it is, or is under, a declared record of some mechanism.** That dissolves my fork: not the check's data, not the entry file's — derived from the declarations, which is what the shape is for.

Two consequences, and the second is the catch:

- **Until the mechanisms are declared, the check needs a holding allowlist** — each undeclared convention named with the ticket that will declare it, every row a straw dog. Same pattern as `.0050`'s allowlist for skills nobody claims: a gap held as a declaration instead of silence. It empties as 01-0017 declares mechanisms.
- **The derivation can't be mechanical yet.** The record declaration is prose today ("one ticket file under `docs/tickets/`"); `record-bearing` becomes a parsed field under [01-0017.0010](docs/tickets/01-0017.0010-terms-defined-before-they-land.md). Until then even the ticket mechanism's rows go in the holding list, and the check reads declarations the day the field parses.

**Recommendation:** adopt the rule as stated; the check ships with the holding allowlist wrapped on 01-0017 and 01-0017.0010, and the rule lands in [Core and instance](AGENTS.md#core-and-instance) in place of the two examples — *a path convention the harness imposes* becomes *a declared record of a mechanism*. Confirm?

# Entry contract

Entry contract: v9, 2026-09-20.

Open your first reply of every session with the `Entry contract:` line above, verbatim.

<straw-dog until="01-0020 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0020-pacer.md">

</straw-dog>

<project-local>
This repository develops the shared dev harness using its own loop. Terms: docs/glossary.md, this
project's own; the method's are .agents/glossary.md's.
What each version of this contract changed: docs/research/entry-contract-findings.md.
</project-local>

## General rules

A **shape** is whatever is under consideration, held between an idea and a thing: formed enough
to have a context and a structure, not yet exhausted by any one realization. Being a shape says
nothing about being load-bearing — an implementation method is a shape too. → [glossary](.agents/glossary.md).

- Do not generalize from one shape. Preserve a seam. Generalize only when a second materially different shape forces the same concept.
- Explore shape context - what is the shape one of? what are its relationships? does its scope overlap any other shape?
- Explore shape structure - how this shape is/can be built? does expanding its structure change the contract or even what the shape is?

- Changing how the work is done — a skill, a check, a record, the loop — is mechanism work: use [/mechanism](.agents/skills/mechanism/SKILL.md). Building what the project produces is not.

- An `<installed>` block in a file is not that file's to edit. Change the rule in the rules file of the mechanism named on the block, and re-install.

- Recency for evidence, longevity for principles.

## Core and instance

`docs/` is substituted whole in a harness instance: a recipient project replaces its contents with
its own.

<project-local>
This repository's own architecture and progress live in docs/ like any other project's — the
instance half doing its job, not a leak.
</project-local>

What core may not do is **depend** on it. Nothing under `.agents/` may reference a file in `docs/`,
or rely on one for its instruction or for any separable part of its own functioning. Naming a path
convention the harness imposes — `docs/tickets/`, `docs/glossary.md` — is not a reference to a
file; pointing at a document only this project has is. Content inside a
[`<project-local>`](#project-local) block is the instance's, not core's. A `<straw-dog>` exempts
nothing: its wrapper is stripped on install and whatever it wrapped ships.

## Document load-bearing, code&comment the rest

A project's architecture, ADRs and glossary are the home for:
- Constitution — identity semantics, consistency model, source-of-truth rules
- Structure — service boundaries, data ownership, event/data flows, extension seams
- Load-bearing — see the definition below

A decision forms in its owning ticket and lands in one of these when it is ready. A decision about a
mechanism lands in that mechanism's doc, and what was refuted in its evidence.

<straw-dog until="01-0012 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0012-hierarchy-coherent.md">
Bad architectural documentation:
- Forecasts are stored in MongoDB collection forecast_hourly.

Better:
- Historical forecast issues must remain independently addressable by (location, valid_time, issue_time) because validation compares what was known at different issue times.
</straw-dog>

## What makes a thing "load-bearing"

- A decision or invariant whose violation would cause multiple parts of the system to become wrong, not merely require local refactoring.
- A thing is load-bearing when several of these are true: has high blast radius, crosses boundaries (i.e. services, persistence, APIs, ownership), other decisions depend on it, it protects an invariant,
is expensive to reverse, holds non-obvious rationale, long-standing.

- Counter-test: if it can be changed locally without understanding the rest of the architecture, it is not load-bearing.

## The loop

Two rings, joined at /align.

    session:   wake with /recall → /align → /conclude → (next session)
    delivery:  /ticket → /plan → /implement → /verify → /maintain → /ticket

/align opens the delivery ring and is where it returns whenever a decision is needed:
/spec for load-bearing shapes, /plan when the governing docs contradict, /verify when a finding needs one, /maintain when maintenance surfaces one. /ticket⇄/plan and /implement⇄/verify iterate as pairs.

Human checkpoints: every decision at /align; spec accepted; breakdown approved; commit; push;
next cycle at /maintain → /ticket.

Do not reopen an accepted decision without new evidence.

### Helpers

- /impact determines the scope and load-bearingness of the shape. Use it to evaluate work volume and its ticketing shape (spec for load-bearing work, tickets for mechanical), work units slicing or whether a shape deserves further investigation due to hidden complexity.
- /discover to investigate hidden complexity, by detecting what else the shape is.
- /dream is an experimental second "lobe" of the harness, aiming to reassess load-bearingness. It is optional, runs after /conclude, and writes dreams that /maintain and /align may pick up; it never amends rules.

## Self-improvement

<straw-dog until="01-0019 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0019-harness-amends-itself-by-explicit-meta-rules.md">
- The rule was present and did not fire - usually means the rule was phrased wrong. This is a call for registration and rephrasing it - write rule failure to docs/rule-failures.md (or strike if exists) and suggests way to amend the rule to capture (use /mechanism and /skill-up for ideas)
- Keeping the register: an entry names the rules that were in play and proposes the amendment; a repeat strikes the entry it repeats rather than opening a second; an entry closes when its amendment lands, or is refused with its reason. Nothing here authorises deleting a rule.
</straw-dog>

## Autonomy

The project sets each switch in its local block below; skills defer to those values.

| Switch | Meaning |
|---|---|
| commit | `ask`: commit only on explicit permission, per change. `auto`: commit when the work is verified. |
| push | `ask`: separate from commit, per push. `never`, `auto`. |
| next-cycle | `ask`: starting the next ticket after one lands needs a nod. `auto`. |
| breakdown | `ask`: a /ticket split needs approval before minting. `auto`. |
| repair | `report`: a clear violation of an explicit rule inside authorized work is fixed and reported. `ask`: show it first. |

## Project-local

A recipient replaces every `<project-local>` block with its own → [glossary](.agents/glossary.md).

- Carry one only for a fact that would differ in another project. Harness layout and the switch
  lookup are shared.
- One block per local fact, beside the rule it answers.
- An unavoidable core reference into `docs/` goes in one, so it does not travel.

## Straw dogs

Wrap anything a live ticket will change, as you write it:
`<straw-dog until="condition" ticket="path">`, or in code a `TODO` naming the ticket. Treat *not
yet*, *until*, *once it exists*, *for now*, *untested* in your own text as the same signal: find
the ticket, or mint one. Wrap at the authored home, never where the harness installs or derives it.
Make the condition testable and the ticket path repository-relative. Leave what no ticket would
change unwrapped.

Follow a straw dog like any other rule until its condition is visibly met; then act on reality,
report the stale block, and do not treat the contradiction as a violation.

<project-local>
commit=ask · push=ask · next-cycle=ask · breakdown=ask · repair=report
</project-local>

# Core stands alone, and a check says so at home

- **Status:** Ready (own align precedes)
- **Type:** HITL
- **Blocks:** [01-0010.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md) and
  [01-0010.0130](./01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md) — accounting for every
  `docs/` reference in core is a precondition to the local-rules design *(the user, 2026-09-10)*:
  none survives deployment unless it is a painted door
- **Related:** [01-0011.0050](./01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md) — its align owns the form of a
  `not yet` referent, and with it how any core text names a ticket — 34 of this ticket's 50
  findings *(27 and 11 until 2026-09-20, when straw-dog content joined the count)*;
  [01-0017](./01-0017-io-graph-coherent.md) — *checking links outside a close* is a `not yet` row
  on `/maintain` naming it
- **Outcome:** A reference from core into the instance half fails at home, on every change, instead
  of on the next port: the tree states which reaches out of `.agents/` are legitimate, a check in
  the verification set holds every core file to that statement, and the references that are not
  legitimate are gone.

## Parent

[Shared harness across projects](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md), whose contract
promises projects "receive accepted changes mechanically while preserving project-specific
behavior" — which requires that what travels can survive the trip.
`/impact`: [the 2026-09-10 assessment](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#impact--2026-09-10).

## The origin cannot violate its own prohibition visibly

*Core and instance* has been a rule since 2026-09-07 and
[ADR-0002](../adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md) has recorded it since
2026-09-09. Both were obeyed by review and broken by construction: in this repository every
`docs/` reference resolves, because core and instance are the same tree. The
[frost_map probe](../research/separation-probe-frost-map.md) produced 35 diagnostics on day one,
this one defect behind 28 instances (14 of them among the 35 — corrected 2026-09-11 on the probe
record), and the probe's count *missed* the four in `/verify` and `/implement`
that a link resolver finds immediately.

The [2026-09-10 `/discover`](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#discover--the-premise-2026-09-10)
named the general form as its most actionable claim, family C: a prohibition the origin environment
cannot violate visibly is not enforced by review, and the remedy is not a better reviewer but a
configuration where **origin equals recipient** — so that what resolves only because the
neighbouring tree happened to be present fails on every change rather than on every port. It is the
same reason dynamic scoping was abandoned.

**What is deliberately not a defect.** The 47 inline path conventions — `docs/tickets/`,
`docs/glossary.md`, `docs/adr/` and their siblings. *Core and instance* permits them in as many
words, and a recipient creates those paths on arrival. Nor is the instance-side `evidence` bullet:
[MECHANISM-FORMAT](../../.agents/skills/mechanism/MECHANISM-FORMAT.md) puts it inside the
`<project-local>` block on purpose. The defect is a core file naming a *particular* instance
document outside any exemption.

## What to build

- ~~**A statement of what may reach out, before any check.**~~ **Resolved 2026-09-20, the align
  *(the user)*: there is no exemption list.** Two facts do the work, and both are already in
  [*Core and instance*](../../AGENTS.md#core-and-instance): a path convention the harness imposes
  is not a reference, and content inside an instance-owned block — `<project-local>` today,
  `<installed by="local">` once [01-0010.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md) retires
  the tag — is not core's. The checker reads the enclosing block mechanically and skips it; the only
  judgment it makes is the convention boundary. **A `<straw-dog>` exempts nothing** — the shear
  strips the wrapper and ships what it wrapped, so a `docs/` link inside one dangled in every
  recipient; the entry file, [ADR-0002](../adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md)
  and the install spec's test bullet said the opposite until today and now agree. That raises the
  count from 27 to **50**: the 23 links inside straw dogs are violations too, and 34 of the 50
  name a ticket.
- **A check in the [verification set](../process.md#verification)** that reads every file under
  `.agents/` and reports each reference reaching outside it with the exemption it claims, or none.
  It reports classes, not a count: the four kinds pull in different directions and a total hides
  which one moved.
- **The contradiction between two core documents resolved.** MECHANISM-FORMAT mandates a markdown
  link for a `not yet` referent; *Core and instance* forbids that link. One of them changes.
  [01-0011.0050](./01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md)'s align owns the referent's form and this one
  must not settle it ahead of that ticket — it takes the answer and enforces it.
- **The references that are not legitimate, removed.** `docs/process.md` is not a convention: it
  is 01-0020's straw dog, whole *(the user, 2026-09-20 — the wrapper covers its first paragraph,
  the claim covers the file)*, and it holds harness rules in the half a recipient replaces — the
  one recipient has a `## Verification` of its own and no `## Autonomy and repair` at all. **This
  ticket moves the rules out** *(the user, 2026-09-20; the pacer's straw dog already says each
  step's rules belong in the step's skill, so nothing of the pacer's is pre-empted)*: the
  definition of a verification set goes into `/verify`'s body and `/implement` links `/verify`;
  the repair policy's four conditions go under the `repair` switch in
  [AGENTS.md § Autonomy](../../AGENTS.md#autonomy), whose semantics they are; this project's
  four commands go into a `<project-local>` block beside the switch block, for
  [.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md) to convert with the rest. `process.md` keeps
  the sequence sketch, wrapped whole, and no core file links it — `/verify` ×3, `/implement` ×1
  and `/maintain`'s block ×1 all repoint. The grading-prose links in the mechanism docs are
  `/maintain`'s R3 (*move story out of a doc into its evidence*) and are routed there rather than
  repaired here.
- **The check fails the run**, not warns. A reporting-only check is the review it replaces.

## Open issues

- **Whether the check is a link resolver or a hermetic run.** Copying `.agents/` alone into an
  empty tree and running every script there is the stronger instrument — it catches what a link
  resolver cannot, such as a script reaching for a path it builds at runtime — but `mechanisms.py`
  cannot pass in that tree today, because evidence is instance-side by design. The stronger form
  needs the align to say what a hermetic tree is *expected* to contain. Cannot be answered before
  the exemption vocabulary exists.
- ~~**Whether a `<straw-dog>` may exempt a reference at all.**~~ **No** *(the user, 2026-09-20)* —
  see *What to build*. The wrapper's own `ticket="…"` attribute is not a shipped reference, since
  the shear removes it; the content is.
- ~~**Whether this tree can grade the check.**~~ It grades the claim actually made — zero and stays
  zero — by a behavioral test that plants a reference and watches the run fail; the install spec's
  testing decisions already say so (2026-09-14). Whether separation *holds* is graded by the
  installer in a recipient, not here.
- **Sequencing** *(the user, 2026-09-20)*: 34 of the 50 violations name a ticket, and how core
  text names a ticket without linking into `docs/` is
  [01-0011.0050](./01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md)'s align. That align runs before this ticket is
  planned; this ticket's RFC implements both answers. The check cannot enter the verification set
  green before then.

## Acceptance criteria — provisional until the align

- [ ] The checker cites [*Core and instance*](../../AGENTS.md#core-and-instance) for what a
      reference is and what instance ownership excludes, rather than restating either.
- [ ] A check enumerates every reference from a file under `.agents/` to a path outside it, and
      reports each as a path convention, as instance-owned content it skipped, or as a diagnostic.
- [ ] Those three kinds are distinguishable in the output, not collapsed into a total; a link
      inside a `<straw-dog>` is a diagnostic like any other.
- [ ] A diagnostic fails the run; the check is in the project's verification set.
- [ ] The check reports zero diagnostics: no core file links `docs/process.md`, the verification
      definition and the repair policy live in core, this project's commands sit in an
      instance-owned block, and the grading-prose links are routed to `/maintain`.
- [ ] A reference added to a core file outside every exemption fails the check — demonstrated by a
      behavioral test that adds one, not by inspection.
- [ ] `/verify` has been run on this ticket against its ticket, RFC, and governing docs.

## Out of scope

The installer and the core revision — [01-0010.0130](./01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md).
What a `<project-local>` block *is* — [01-0010.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md).
The form of a `not yet` referent — [01-0011.0050](./01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md). Whether every
installed skill is named by a mechanism — [01-0017](./01-0017-io-graph-coherent.md). Repairing the
grading prose in the three mechanism docs, which is `/maintain`'s R3 over those records.

## Parent scope addressed

as success.

Concretely:

**What it does.** One script, `core_stands_alone.py --check` (name is the RFC's). It walks every `.md` and every non-test `.py` under `.agents/`. In each file it finds two things: markdown link targets, and path literals that start with `docs/`, `AGENTS.md` or a host stub. For each one it answers three questions in order:

1. Is this line inside a `<project-local>` or `<installed by="local">` block? → **skipped**, instance-owned.
2. Does the path resolve to a place on the list — a declared directory itself, or a declared file? → **place**.
3. Otherwise → **diagnostic**: file, line, the path, and which of the three it is not.

It prints the three classes with counts and every diagnostic's location, and exits non-zero on any diagnostic. A `<straw-dog>` is not one of the questions — a link inside one falls through to 2 and 3 like any other line.

On today's tree it would report 50 diagnostics; after this ticket's moves (`process.md` links out, evidence and grading links to `/maintain`) and `.0050`'s answer for the 34 ticket-naming links, zero.

**When it runs.** It joins the four commands in the verification set — so at `/verify` on every ticket, and whenever `/implement` runs the named checks during work. It is not a hook and not on commit; nothing in this project runs on commit today, and I'm not proposing to change that here. The "on every change" in the ticket's outcome means *every change that reaches `/verify`*, which is every change that lands.

The behavioral test for it plants a link from a core file to `docs/tickets/x.md` in a temp tree and asserts the run fails; plants `docs/tickets/` and asserts it passes; plants a link inside `<project-local>` and asserts it's skipped.

**Decisive fact:** the check's inputs are record declarations, and *a mechanism declares its records* is mechanism-shape's rule ([MECHANISM-FORMAT § Records](.agents/skills/mechanism/MECHANISM-FORMAT.md)). # Entry contract

Entry contract: v9, 2026-09-20.

Open your first reply of every session with the `Entry contract:` line above, verbatim.

<straw-dog until="01-0020 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0020-pacer.md">
Run /recall first in every session, whatever the first message says.
</straw-dog>

<project-local>
This repository develops the shared dev harness using its own loop. Terms: docs/glossary.md, this
project's own; the method's are .agents/glossary.md's.
What each version of this contract changed: docs/research/entry-contract-findings.md.
</project-local>

## General rules

A **shape** is whatever is under consideration, held between an idea and a thing: formed enough
to have a context and a structure, not yet exhausted by any one realization. Being a shape says
nothing about being load-bearing — an implementation method is a shape too. → [glossary](.agents/glossary.md).

- Do not generalize from one shape. Preserve a seam. Generalize only when a second materially different shape forces the same concept.
- Explore shape context - what is the shape one of? what are its relationships? does its scope overlap any other shape?
- Explore shape structure - how this shape is/can be built? does expanding its structure change the contract or even what the shape is?

- Changing how the work is done — a skill, a check, a record, the loop — is mechanism work: use [/mechanism](.agents/skills/mechanism/SKILL.md). Building what the project produces is not.

- An `<installed>` block in a file is not that file's to edit. Change the rule in the rules file of the mechanism named on the block, and re-install.

- Recency for evidence, longevity for principles.

## Core and instance

`docs/` is substituted whole in a harness instance: a recipient project replaces its contents with
its own.

<project-local>
This repository's own architecture and progress live in docs/ like any other project's — the
instance half doing its job, not a leak.
</project-local>

What core may not do is **depend** on it. Nothing under `.agents/` may reference a file in `docs/`,
or rely on one for its instruction or for any separable part of its own functioning. A core file
may name a path under `docs/` only when that path is a record a mechanism declares — the directory
that holds a kind of record, or a file that is one — never a particular record inside such a
directory: `docs/tickets/` and `docs/glossary.md` are places, `docs/tickets/01-0020-pacer.md` is a
document only this project has. Content inside a
[`<project-local>`](#project-local) block is the instance's, not core's. A `<straw-dog>` exempts
nothing: its wrapper is stripped on install and whatever it wrapped ships.

## Document load-bearing, code&comment the rest

A project's architecture, ADRs and glossary are the home for:
- Constitution — identity semantics, consistency model, source-of-truth rules
- Structure — service boundaries, data ownership, event/data flows, extension seams
- Load-bearing — see the definition below

A decision forms in its owning ticket and lands in one of these when it is ready. A decision about a
mechanism lands in that mechanism's doc, and what was refuted in its evidence.

<straw-dog until="01-0012 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0012-hierarchy-coherent.md">
Bad architectural documentation:
- Forecasts are stored in MongoDB collection forecast_hourly.

Better:
- Historical forecast issues must remain independently addressable by (location, valid_time, issue_time) because validation compares what was known at different issue times.
</straw-dog>

## What makes a thing "load-bearing"

- A decision or invariant whose violation would cause multiple parts of the system to become wrong, not merely require local refactoring.
- A thing is load-bearing when several of these are true: has high blast radius, crosses boundaries (i.e. services, persistence, APIs, ownership), other decisions depend on it, it protects an invariant,
is expensive to reverse, holds non-obvious rationale, long-standing.

- Counter-test: if it can be changed locally without understanding the rest of the architecture, it is not load-bearing.

## The loop

Two rings, joined at /align.

    session:   wake with /recall → /align → /conclude → (next session)
    delivery:  /ticket → /plan → /implement → /verify → /maintain → /ticket

/align opens the delivery ring and is where it returns whenever a decision is needed:
/spec for load-bearing shapes, /plan when the governing docs contradict, /verify when a finding needs one, /maintain when maintenance surfaces one. /ticket⇄/plan and /implement⇄/verify iterate as pairs.

Human checkpoints: every decision at /align; spec accepted; breakdown approved; commit; push;
next cycle at /maintain → /ticket.

Do not reopen an accepted decision without new evidence.

### Helpers

- /impact determines the scope and load-bearingness of the shape. Use it to evaluate work volume and its ticketing shape (spec for load-bearing work, tickets for mechanical), work units slicing or whether a shape deserves further investigation due to hidden complexity.
- /discover to investigate hidden complexity, by detecting what else the shape is.
- /dream is an experimental second "lobe" of the harness, aiming to reassess load-bearingness. It is optional, runs after /conclude, and writes dreams that /maintain and /align may pick up; it never amends rules.

## Self-improvement

<straw-dog until="01-0019 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0019-harness-amends-itself-by-explicit-meta-rules.md">
- The rule was present and did not fire - usually means the rule was phrased wrong. This is a call for registration and rephrasing it - write rule failure to docs/rule-failures.md (or strike if exists) and suggests way to amend the rule to capture (use /mechanism and /skill-up for ideas)
- Keeping the register: an entry names the rules that were in play and proposes the amendment; a repeat strikes the entry it repeats rather than opening a second; an entry closes when its amendment lands, or is refused with its reason. Nothing here authorises deleting a rule.
</straw-dog>

## Autonomy

The project sets each switch in its local block below; skills defer to those values.

| Switch | Meaning |
|---|---|
| commit | `ask`: commit only on explicit permission, per change. `auto`: commit when the work is verified. |
| push | `ask`: separate from commit, per push. `never`, `auto`. |
| next-cycle | `ask`: starting the next ticket after one lands needs a nod. `auto`. |
| breakdown | `ask`: a /ticket split needs approval before minting. `auto`. |
| repair | `report`: a clear violation of an explicit rule inside authorized work is fixed and reported. `ask`: show it first. |

## Project-local

A recipient replaces every `<project-local>` block with its own → [glossary](.agents/glossary.md).

- Carry one only for a fact that would differ in another project. Harness layout and the switch
  lookup are shared.
- One block per local fact, beside the rule it answers.
- An unavoidable core reference into `docs/` goes in one, so it does not travel.

## Straw dogs

Wrap anything a live ticket will change, as you write it:
`<straw-dog until="condition" ticket="path">`, or in code a `TODO` naming the ticket. Treat *not
yet*, *until*, *once it exists*, *for now*, *untested* in your own text as the same signal: find
the ticket, or mint one. Wrap at the authored home, never where the harness installs or derives it.
Make the condition testable and the ticket path repository-relative. Leave what no ticket would
change unwrapped.

Follow a straw dog like any other rule until its condition is visibly met; then act on reality,
report the stale block, and do not treat the contradiction as a violation.

<project-local>
commit=ask · push=ask · next-cycle=ask · breakdown=ask · repair=report
</project-local>

Yes — and the tree already answers which way. Scripts sit flat in `.agents/scripts/` with no owner in their names; ownership lives in the parts tables only. What relates a script to its mechanism today is the **register it walks**: `tickets.py` walks tickets, `mechanisms.py` walks the mechanism set, `straw_dogs.py` walks straw dogs. So the name is already taken, correctly:

**`mechanisms.py --check` gains the leak check.** No new script, no new name to settle; the parts table row is the one that exists; *leak* stays as the diagnostic class in the output (`0 leaks · 118 places · 15 instance-owned`) and as the glossary term. The verification set doesn't grow by a command either.

By location — `.agents/scripts/mechanism-shape/…` — would be a second convention for six scripts that follow the first; not for one check.

One cost to name: `mechanisms.py --check` can't go green here until `.0050` settles the 34 ticket-naming links — so for that stretch the whole mechanism check fails, not a new command nobody depends on yet. # Core stands alone, and a check says so at home

- **Status:** Planned (aligned 2026-09-20; 01-0011.0050's align precedes /plan)
- **Type:** HITL
- **Blocks:** [01-0010.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md) and
  [01-0010.0130](./01-0010.0130-harness-installs-into-another-tree.md) — accounting for every
  `docs/` reference in core is a precondition to the local-rules design *(the user, 2026-09-10)*:
  none survives deployment unless it is a painted door
- **Related:** [01-0011.0050](./01-0011.0050-shape-checked.md) — its align owns the form of a
  `not yet` referent, and with it how any core text names a ticket — 34 of this ticket's 50
  findings *(27 and 11 until 2026-09-20, when straw-dog content joined the count)*;
  [01-0017](./01-0017-io-graph-coherent.md) — *checking links outside a close* is a `not yet` row
  on `/maintain` naming it
- **Outcome:** A reference from core into the instance half fails at home, on every change, instead
  of on the next port: the tree states which reaches out of `.agents/` are legitimate, a check in
  the verification set holds every core file to that statement, and the references that are not
  legitimate are gone.

...
## The origin cannot violate its own prohibition visibly

*Core and instance* has been a rule since 2026-09-07 and
[ADR-0002](../adr/0002-core-may-not-depend-on-the-instance-half.md) has recorded it since
2026-09-09. Both were obeyed by review and broken by construction: in this repository every
`docs/` reference resolves, because core and instance are the same tree. The
[frost_map probe](../research/separation-probe-frost-map.md) produced 35 diagnostics on day one,
this one defect behind 28 instances (14 of them among the 35 — corrected 2026-09-11 on the probe
record), and the probe's count *missed* the four in `/verify` and `/implement`
that a link resolver finds immediately.

The [2026-09-10 `/discover`](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#discover--the-premise-2026-09-10)
named the general form as its most actionable claim, family C: a prohibition the origin environment
cannot violate visibly is not enforced by review, and the remedy is not a better reviewer but a
configuration where **origin equals recipient** — so that what resolves only because the
neighbouring tree happened to be present fails on every change rather than on every port. It is the
same reason dynamic scoping was abandoned.

**What is deliberately not a defect.** The 47 inline path conventions — `docs/tickets/`,
`docs/glossary.md`, `docs/adr/` and their siblings. *Core and instance* permits them in as many
words, and a recipient creates those paths on arrival. Nor is the instance-side `evidence` bullet:
[MECHANISM-FORMAT](../../.agents/skills/mechanism/MECHANISM-FORMAT.md) puts it inside the
`<project-local>` block on purpose. The defect is a core file naming a *particular* instance
document outside any exemption.

Base directory for this skill: D:\Dev\AI\agents\.claude\skills\commit

- Commit the work in current session only. Do not commit changes of other session that might represent a work in progress. When in doubt, ask user.

- Look at pending changes; group them by content aligning with origin topic, ticket, rfc or change type (docs/code/cicd/skills).

- Separate implementation and documentation commits.

- Prefix the subject with the loop step that produced the work, uppercase, then a colon:
  `ALIGN`, `SPEC`, `TICKET`, `PLAN`, `IMPLEMENT`, `VERIFY`, `MAINTAIN`, `DISCOVER`, `RECALL`,
  `CONCLUDE`. Three sit outside the ring: `FIX` for a repair taken on its own, `EQUIP` for
  a change to the harness's own installation, and `DREAM` for a record the second lobe wrote. One
  prefix per commit — where the work spans two steps, take the dominant one and name the bleed in
  the message. The prefix says which step produced the work, never which files it touched: what
  changed is visible in the diff, and which step produced it is not.

- In case the file changes belong to several groups, commit the file with the group forming its dominant topic and mention the bleed in that commit's message.

- Do not reference sessions in commit comments, sessions are ephemeral.

- Unless already working in branch or instructed to branch - commit to default branch.

- When committing a code change, first run the checks the repository defines for itself — its
  linter, its formatter in check mode, its type checker, its tests. Pure doc changes need none
  of them. **Read them from where the project states them; never carry them here.** A commit
  skill holding a project's commands is a second home for them, and it is wrong for every
  project but the one it was written in.

- Do not commit without explicit instruction or permission from user.
- Separately, do not push without explicit instruction or permission from user.
